matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer provides implicit freshness

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer provides implicit freshness
findings.rationale: The old GET endpoint attempted a live GitHub fetch on every call (with a fallback to persisted data on failure). The new GET always serves the persisted DB state without any GitHub call. Callers that relied on GET returning fresh data (e.g., after a PR was updated on GitHub) will now see stale data until they explicitly call POST /pulls/:id/refresh. This narrows what callers can depend on without a code change on their side.

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer refreshes data from GitHub

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer refreshes data from GitHub
findings.rationale: The old GET handler attempted a live GitHub refresh (with a silent fallback to the database). The new handler always serves the persisted database state without any GitHub call. Existing callers (e.g., CI runner, e2e tests, external consumers) that relied on the implicit refresh to get fresh data will now receive stale data until they explicitly call the new POST /pulls/:id/refresh endpoint. The response shape is identical, so no caller fails, but the contract narrows what callers can rely on.

findings.title: useRefreshPull hook captures stale prId in closure
findings.rationale: The `useMutation` callback `mutationFn: () => api.post(...)` captures `prId` from the closure at the time the hook is called. If the component re-renders with a different `prId`, the mutation will still use the original `prId`, potentially refreshing the wrong pull request. Additionally, if `prId` is null/undefined, the URL becomes `/pulls/null/refresh` or `/pulls/undefined/refresh`.

findings.title: Import path may not resolve without a barrel export
findings.rationale: The import `from "../../../../../../../lib/hooks"` expects a file `hooks/index.ts` or `hooks.ts` that re-exports `useRefreshPull`. The hook is defined in `core.ts`. If no barrel export exists, this import will fail at build time.

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer refreshes data from GitHub

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer refreshes data from GitHub
findings.rationale: The GET handler previously attempted to fetch the latest files, commits, and body from GitHub and update the database before returning the PR detail. Now it only reads from the database with no side effects. Callers that relied on the implicit refresh (e.g., automated scripts or the PR list view that depended on backfilled diff stats) will silently receive stale data until they explicitly call POST /pulls/:id/refresh. This narrows the contract: the endpoint no longer guarantees fresh data. The compatible alternative is to use the new POST /pulls/:id/refresh endpoint to explicitly refresh data before reading.

findings.title: Misleading comment in GET route
findings.rationale: The comment says 'Pure read now — no GitHub call, no DB write. Call POST /pulls/:id/refresh first to pull the latest files/commits/body before viewing a PR.' This is accurate but could be clearer: it implies the caller should call POST before GET, but the GET route itself does not enforce or suggest that. Consider rewording to 'GET is a pure read; use POST /pulls/:id/refresh to update from GitHub.'

matched_title: New field `reviewUrl` breaks the existing snake_case convention

findings.title: New field `reviewUrl` breaks the existing snake_case convention
findings.rationale: All other fields in `PrMeta` use snake_case (e.g., `cost_usd`, `latest_findings`). Adding a camelCase field (`reviewUrl`) introduces inconsistency. While no caller breaks today, it narrows what callers can rely on — they can no longer assume all keys are snake_case. This could cause confusion or bugs if clients use a mapping that expects snake_case.

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id response drops fields previously returned from GitHub

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id response drops fields previously returned from GitHub
findings.rationale: The old GET route returned `{ ...detail, id: pr.id }` where `detail` was the full GitHub PR object (including fields like `mergeable`, `draft`, `labels`, `head`, `base`, `user`, etc.). The new route returns only a fixed set of fields (id, number, title, author, branch, base, head_sha, additions, deletions, files_count, status, opened_at, updated_at, body, files, commits). Any caller that accesses the dropped fields will now receive `undefined` or a runtime error. This is a breaking contract change.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer falls back to DB on GitHub fetch failure
findings.rationale: The old route had a try-catch that logged a warning and served DB data if the GitHub fetch failed. The new route removes the GitHub fetch entirely, so if the DB query itself fails (e.g., connection issue), the error propagates as a 500 instead of returning a partial response. This changes the error contract for callers that previously received a 200 with DB data on transient failures.

findings.title: POST /pulls/:id/refresh lacks error handling for GitHub fetch failure
findings.rationale: The new POST route calls `gh.getPullRequest` without a try-catch. If the GitHub API call fails (rate limit, network error, token expired), the route will throw an unhandled error, resulting in a 500 response. The client mutation does not appear to handle this gracefully (no error toast or retry).

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer returns `html_url` (and other GitHub API fields)

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer returns `html_url` (and other GitHub API fields)
findings.rationale: The old GET handler returned `{ ...detail, id: pr.id }` where `detail` was the full GitHub API response, including `html_url`, `state`, `labels`, etc. The new handler returns only the explicitly listed fields. The client's 'View on GitHub' button (visible in the diff context) uses `pr.html_url` to open the PR on GitHub. With this change, `html_url` is never present in the GET response, so the button will either break or open an undefined URL. This is a breaking change for any caller that relied on any field from the GitHub API payload that is no longer returned.

findings.title: Type mismatch in `useRefreshPull` hook parameter
findings.rationale: The `useRefreshPull` hook declares `prId: string | null | undefined`, but the component passes `prId` which is likely a number (from route params). This will cause a TypeScript error in strict mode. The API endpoint accepts a numeric ID in the path, so string coercion works at runtime, but the type annotation should be widened to `string | number | null | undefined` or the component should convert the value.

matched_title: New field uses camelCase while the rest of the schema uses snake_case

findings.title: New field uses camelCase while the rest of the schema uses snake_case
findings.rationale: The existing fields in `PrMeta` (e.g., `cost_usd`, `latest_findings`, `score`) all use snake_case. The new field `reviewUrl` breaks this convention. While no existing caller depends on the new field, the inconsistency will confuse consumers that rely on automated mapping (e.g., camelCase-to-snake_case transforms) and sets a bad precedent for future additions. Rename to `review_url` to match the rest of the schema.
